title: Java object lifecycle from creation to garbage collection
answer: An object's lifecycle begins with class availability and object creation: memory is allocated, fields receive default values, initialization and constructor logic run, and a reference becomes available to application code. The object remains reachable while strong references can reach it. When it becomes unreachable, it becomes eligible for garbage collection, but collection timing is not guaranteed. The JVM may reclaim its memory later. For external resources, do not rely on GC; use deterministic cleanup such as `AutoCloseable`, try-with-resources, framework lifecycle hooks, or cleaners only as a fallback safety mechanism.
